newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Most S.Korea Kia shares fall on lack of new loans.
newsitem.headline: Most S.Korea Kia shares fall on lack of new loans.

text.p: Most shares of South Korea's Kia Group affiliates fell in early trading on investors' disappointment over the news that immediate emergency loans to the troubled group were unlikely, brokers said on Tuesday.
Kia Motors lost 900 won to 14,300, Asia Motors fell 340 won to 5,110, Kisan shed 200 to 5,410, Kia Precision dropped 340 to 8,200 and Kia Service fell 350 to 5,150.
"Investors are frustrated over conditional emergency loans, which they think would be unlikely to be provided in the near future," said Park Joo-chang of Daewoo Securities.

Creditor banks to Kia Group on Monday agreed to grant 183.1 billion won in emergency loans but only if presidents of Kia affiliates tendered resignations and the labour union agreed in writing to freeze their wages and cut employees.
Creditors unanimously agreed the bailout protection period for the nation's eighth largest conglomerate would continue until September 29 without condition.

Brokers said Kia Steel hit its upper daily limit for the fourth straight day, rising 230 won to 3,140. It has been rising on last week's news that Hyundai Motor Co and Daewoo Motor Co have agreed in principle to buy stakes in Kia Steel.
However, other Kia shares were expected to remain weak for the rest of the day, brokers said.
